title: LED Inspection - Corrosion Detection on Teron 640
subtitle: Post-Clean Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Lisa Johansson

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron 640 system to detect and classify Corrosion defects during post-clean inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Corrosion defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron 640 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron 640
- Inspection Type: LED Inspection
- Target Defect: Corrosion
- Process Step: Post-Clean
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all Teron 640 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for post-clean monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron 640
Software Version: v13.4.998
Recipe: LED_INSPECTION_14nm_POST_CLEAN
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (73 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron 640 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'LED Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Corrosion defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 55 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.6% for LED Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-02-05
Wafers Tested: 5
Total Defects Found: 3608
Defect Density: 1148.46 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.1%
Capture Rate: 95.2%
Test Duration: 103 minutes
System Uptime: 96.9%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron 640 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Corrosion at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
